name: Vanishing White Matter Disease Adult Form
aliases: Adult-onset Childhood Ataxia with Central Nervous System Hypomyelination (CACH)

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Vanishing White Matter Disease Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Progressive neurological decline with episodes triggered by stressors such as fever or head trauma
Characteristic MRI findings showing diffuse white matter rarefaction and cystic degeneration
Identification of pathogenic biallelic mutations in EIF2B1-5 genes

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of progressive neurological decline with stress-induced episodes, characteristic MRI findings, and confirmation of biallelic EIF2B mutations
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires integration of clinical, radiological, and genetic data.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Diffuse white matter rarefaction on MRI

rare.symptomName: Endocrine dysfunction (e.g., ovarian failure in females)

laboratory: Possible elevated lactate during stress episodes
imaging: MRI showing diffuse symmetric white matter rarefaction and cystic degeneration
genetic: Biallelic pathogenic variants in EIF2B1, EIF2B2, EIF2B3, EIF2B4, or EIF2B5 genes

distinguishingFeatures: Variable MRI patterns without cystic degeneration
Presence of oligoclonal bands in CSF

redFlags: Rapid neurological deterioration following minor head trauma or febrile illness
MRI showing diffuse cystic white matter changes
references: van der Knaap MS, et al. Vanishing white matter disease: a review. Neurology. 2006.
Bugiani M, et al. Adult-onset vanishing white matter disease: clinical and genetic features. Neurology. 2010.
Orphanet: Vanishing White Matter Disease. https://www.orpha.net
